Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

This keeps `PostCode` as a custom type and routes inputs through its existing normalization and validation without the deprecated hook.

Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).

Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.

Import `Field` from `pydantic` and declare `key: Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right")`. This makes Pydantic v2 try `int` first, so numeric strings such as `"42"` become integers while nonnumeric strings remain strings.

Import `field_validator` from `pydantic` and add a `@field_validator("key", mode="before")` that converts a string to `int` when `value.isdecimal()` is true, returning all other values unchanged. This explicitly converts numeric strings before union validation.
Import ConfigDict from pydantic and set `model_config = ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` on `Label`, allowing Pydantic v2 to coerce numeric SKU values to strings.
Import `field_validator` from pydantic and add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that returns `str(value)` for integer inputs, so numeric SKUs are converted before string validation.

Convert the sensor reading before constructing the model: pass `units=int(reading)` in `from_sensor`. This truncates fractional readings toward zero and keeps `StockLevel.units` as a strict integer field.

Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` that converts numeric inputs with `int(value)` before integer validation, so fractional readings are truncated when constructing `StockLevel`.

Create the patch model, then return the sorted keys of `patch.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`. This preserves explicitly supplied `None` values while excluding fields omitted from the input.
Import `field_serializer` from Pydantic and add a serializer to `Shift` for `started` that returns `value.isoformat()`. This emits `+00:00` for UTC instead of Pydantic's `Z`.
